question.worked_solution:
First we apply the quotient rule, subtracting exponents in the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{q}^{2}\cdot \frac{{q}^{3}}{{q}^{8}} & = \\ {q}^{2}\cdot {q}^{3-8} & = \\ {q}^{2}\cdot {q}^{-5} & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then we apply the product rule, adding exponents in the product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{q}^{2}\cdot {q}^{-5} & = \\ {q}^{2+(-5)} & = \\ {q}^{2-5} & = \\ {q}^{-3} & = \\ \frac{1}{{q}^{3}} & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{q}^{2}\cdot \frac{{q}^{3}}{{q}^{8}}=\frac{1}{{q}^{3}}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
